meta.checked_against: publisher pages, PubMed, arXiv and author PDFs; 'abstract' where only the abstract was reachable

cited.cited_as: Hota and Kumar 2019: farther-apart bases give more workspace for large objects, closer bases for small; longer links help both
cited.source: R. K. Hota, C. S. Kumar, "Effect of hand design and object size on the workspace of three-fingered hands," Mechanism and Machine Theory 133:311-328, 2019. doi:10.1016/j.mechmachtheory.2018.11.011
cited.correction: The object is a cylinder held in a tripod grasp; the under-actuated version of the hand prefers wide bases for every object size.
cited.finding: Fully actuated hand: wide bases maximise the position and orientation workspace for large objects and close bases for small ones; longer links enlarge it for both. No diameters or workspace values in the abstract.

cited.cited_as: Borras and Dollar 2015: maximal workspace when the palm radius is about the object radius plus half a finger length
cited.source: J. Borras, A. M. Dollar, "Dimensional synthesis of three-fingered robot hands for maximal precision manipulation workspace," IJRR 34(14):1731-1746, 2015. doi:10.1177/0278364915608250
cited.correction: none; 'palm radius' is the radius of the circle through the finger bases. Stated as Pr - Or ~ 1 with palm and object diameters in finger lengths.
cited.finding: Three two-link fingers with a base joint about the palm normal, flexion 0-90 deg, round objects, contacts as points with friction. Workspace = reachable object poses out of 4,879 positions x 305 orientations; fully actuated maximum 124,451 poses. Symmetric 120 deg finger spacing and a distal/proximal ratio of 1-1.2 are best. Computation only.

cited.cited_as: Elangovan et al.: link dimensions and interfinger distance optimised; finger-base distance changes the workspace; gripper with reconfigurable bases
cited.source: N. Elangovan, L. Gerez, G. Gao, M. Liarokapis, "Improving robotic manipulation without sacrificing grasping efficiency: a multi-modal, adaptive gripper with reconfigurable finger bases," IEEE Access 9:83298-83308, 2021. doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3086802 (IROS 2021 companion doi:10.1109/IROS51168.2021.9636392)
cited.correction: Two fingers, planar analysis; the optimal inter-finger distance converged to zero in every optimisation case. 'Enlighten' is the Glasgow repository holding the papers.
cited.finding: Workspace shrinks as the two bases separate; no single distance covers the union of the workspaces. Hardware: two tendon fingers on rails at 0, 30, 70 and 110 mm, five spheres of 16-96 mm.

cited.cited_as: RUTH: a two-DoF palm reconfigured to grasp and manipulate objects of different sizes on hardware
cited.source: Q. Lu, N. Baron, A. B. Clark, N. Rojas, "Systematic object-invariant in-hand manipulation via reconfigurable underactuation: introducing the RUTH gripper," IJRR 40(12-14):1402-1418, 2021. doi:10.1177/02783649211048929
cited.finding: A five-bar palm carries three underactuated fingers; moving the palm switches grasp types and moves the held object (57 mm translation, 68 deg rotation) on cylinders of 30-90 mm. The palm is the manipulation mechanism, not a fixed design variable.

cited.cited_as: 2026 variable-stroke soft hand: better grasping when the initial finger spacing matches object size
cited.source: H. Chen, Z. Wang, S. Zhang, L. Yao, "A synchronous variable-stroke mechanism for workspace enhancement of a four-finger soft robotic hand," Biomimetics 11(5):318, 2026. doi:10.3390/biomimetics11050318
cited.correction: One fixed stroke against one hand-set stroke per object; spacing was not swept.
cited.finding: Eight objects of 5-12 cm: grasp success 95.0 % with the per-object stroke against 62.5 % fixed; stable hold 77.5 % against 40.0 %.

cited.cited_as: 2026 reconfigurable dual-opposition hand: object-size-conditioned workspace, rotation across a broad range of sizes
cited.source: W. Su et al., "A reconfigurable dual-opposition architecture for single-hand assembly and manipulation," arXiv:2609.22871, 2026
cited.correction: The wide size range of the rotation result is simulation; the size-conditioned workspace is a force-closure holding set, not a rotation workspace.
cited.finding: PPO policies per sphere diameter, 22 diameters of 40-250 mm, 300 rollouts each: 98.6 % mean success against 73.8 % for the LEAP Hand. Hardware: three balls, one 20 s rollout each. The palm slide is not swept against diameter.

cited.cited_as: Wang, Oh and Pollard 2609.25619: contact-relative representation insensitive to hand kinematics, five hands in simulation
cited.source: S. Wang, J. Oh, N. S. Pollard, "Relative contact velocity-controlled hand-object mechanism for dexterous tool manipulation," arXiv:2609.25619, 2026
cited.correction: none; all results are teleoperated simulation (Drake, hydroelastic contact).
cited.finding: Five hands (Orca V2, Wuji, Sharpa Wave, a three-finger and a five-finger custom hand); cylinder and screwdriver tasks; velocity-tracking RMSE only; hardware listed as future work.

cited.cited_as: Human grip configurations change at common object-size / hand-size ratios across adults and children
cited.source: K. M. Newell et al., Dev. Psychobiol. 22(1):1-13, 1989; K. M. Newell, P. V. McDonald, R. Baillargeon, Dev. Psychobiol. 26(4):195-205, 1993; P. Cesari, K. M. Newell, J. Exp. Psychol. HPP 25(4):927-935, 1999 and 26(5):1657-1668, 2000
cited.correction: Grip configuration means the number of digits and hands used; Cesari and Newell add object mass to the scaling relation.
cited.finding: 31 infants and 31 adults switched from one hand to two at cup diameter / hand length 0.75-0.80, i.e. at about 5.6 cm and 13.8 cm in absolute terms.
cited.checked: PubMed; full text of the 1993 paper

cited.cited_as: Grip force, normal force and contact area depend on handle diameter relative to hand length; the force-maximising grip span grows with hand size
cited.source: N. J. Seo, T. J. Armstrong, Human Factors 50(5):734-744, 2008; Y.-K. Kong, B. D. Lowe, Int. J. Ind. Ergon. 35(6):495-507, 2005; J. Ruiz-Ruiz et al., J. Hand Surg. Am. 27(5):897-901, 2002; J. R. Ruiz et al., J. Hand Surg. Am. 31(8):1367-1372, 2006
cited.correction: Over D/L 0.2-0.5 all three quantities fall monotonically, so there is no peak in the data; the optimal grip span grows with hand size in women, teenagers and children but is a fixed 5.5 cm in adult men.
cited.finding: Fifteen adults, cylinders of 38-83 mm: D/L explains 62, 57 and 71 % of the variance of grip force, normal force and contact area. A force-optimal diameter of about 0.20 L follows from hand geometry.

cited.cited_as: Bullock, Feix and Dollar: human precision-manipulation workspace peaks at an intermediate object size; the smallest objects give the smallest workspace
cited.source: I. M. Bullock, T. Feix, A. M. Dollar, "Human precision manipulation workspace: effects of object size and number of fingers used," IEEE EMBC 2015, pp. 5768-5772. doi:10.1109/EMBC.2015.7319703
cited.correction: The source is the EMBC 2015 paper; the IEEE TBME 2015 paper used a single object size.
cited.finding: Sixteen adults, seven bars of 20-80 mm: normalised workspace 1.23 at 48-59 mm (27-34 % of hand length) against 0.72 at 17-27 mm (10-15 %); only the smallest size differed significantly.

cited.cited_as: Hu et al.: thumbs both too long and too short hurt modelled dexterity
cited.source: D. Hu, C.-H. Xiong, M.-J. Liu, "Exploring the existence of better hands for manipulation than the human hand based on hand proportions," J. Theor. Biol. 440:100-111, 2018. doi:10.1016/j.jtbi.2017.12.026
cited.correction: none; the model has no object size or finger-base spacing.
cited.finding: Kinematic model over anthropoid hand proportions; the best hand has longer metacarpals relative to phalanges than the human hand.

missed.why: In about 10,000 everyday grasps, 96 % of grasped widths were 7 cm or less: the size range a sweep should cover.
Reconfigurable Bricard palm: 3 palm states x 15 objects (17-180 mm), 3 trials each; the latest configuration-by-size table on hardware.

missed.source: K. Fay et al., House of Dextra, ICLR 2026, arXiv:2512.03743
missed.why: Morphology-conditioned co-design in simulation: in-hand rotation correlates with palm-width scale at r = -0.73; object size randomised, not resolved.

verdict: No paper sweeps the finger-base geometry of one physical multi-finger hand through five or more settings against several controlled object sizes, and none compares simulated and measured landscapes at the same points for more than three designs.
